changelog: Role: clarified that marking is generous but the ranking must protect against premature assertions by ensuring the safest candidate(s) are ranked highest; this focuses the model on avoiding placement errors without shrinking candidacy.

Core Principles: added a short, language-neutral positive criterion for high-ranked cuts (prefer cuts that leave a stable predication with core participants) and a reminder to demote (via ranking) candidates that end immediately before tokens likely to continue the phrase — this guides ranking without adding hard forbiddances.

Never Segment: removed the repeated, frozen punctuation/start/end constraints (refer to [Output Rules]) and tightened the forbidden category to only truly impossible splits (non-renderable stretches), avoiding redundant restatement of output-format details.

Examples — Segment: replaced some generic examples with targeted examples illustrating correct segmentation for common placement-failure patterns (agent/voice disambiguation, pronoun/antecedent, multiword adjectival compounds, sentence-boundary segmentation), so the model learns safe placements from examples rather than more prohibitions.

Examples — Do NOT Segment: added realistic Do-NOT lists taken from frequent critic failures (premature cuts before negation, postverbal obliques, relative/complement clauses, short prepositional/temporal fragments, vague pronouns) to show where segmentation should be withheld.
